findings: All 0.5 mm, 0.9 mm, and 1.3 mm lower-rim lifts preserve the 171-pair body self-collision baseline in neutral, open, smile, and frames 1, 20, 33, and 61.
The 0.5 mm variant changes the relaxed aperture too little to justify another corrective key.
The 0.9 mm and 1.3 mm variants create visible bumps along the lower-lip upper rim while leaving the aperture unnaturally dark.
A narrow lower-rim selection cannot reproduce a relaxed mouth closure; both lips and commissures must participate.
decision: Reject all r1111 variants and retain r1110 as the active offline study.
nextAction: Build a broader perioral deformation field over continuous topology with coupled upper-lip, lower-lip, and mouth-corner motion.
